findings.evidence: "## Basic Syntax", "## Domain-Driven Design Patterns", and "## Common Patterns" introduce extensive standard UML syntax and repository/factory/strategy examples. By line count, this reference and the similarly expansive C4 and flowchart catalogs substantially dilute the expert renderer constraints and failure modes.
findings.fix: Condense familiar syntax, UML definitions, and generic design-pattern examples across the class, C4, and flowchart references. Retain compact templates and Mermaid-specific decisions, compatibility constraints, and failure modes; preserve all attribution and source credits.

findings.evidence: "New diagram: apply `authoring-rules.md` sections 2-5 in full" applies flowchart-oriented constraints before classification. Those sections require role-specific shapes and prescribe a palette when there are six or more nodes, although sequence and C4 diagrams do not support the prescribed flowchart shapes and classDef styling. Only the state/Git/Gantt/pie reference explicitly exempts its types.
findings.fix: Scope flowchart shape, subgraph, and classDef requirements explicitly to flowcharts. For sequence, C4, class, ER, and architecture-beta diagrams, use supported type-native layout and styling controls while retaining contrast and semantic-labeling principles. Put these exceptions before the instruction to apply the authoring rules.

findings.evidence: "### Rounded Rectangle" demonstrates `B([Rounded process])`, while "### Stadium/Pill Shape" demonstrates `C(Start or End)`. The examples render the opposite shapes from their headings and disagree with the stadium syntax in authoring-rules.md.
findings.fix: Use `B(Rounded process)` for the rounded rectangle and `C([Start or End])` for the stadium so the shape catalog matches Mermaid syntax and the authoring rules.

findings.evidence: `LineItem "1" --> "1" Product : references` in the e-commerce example models each Product as belonging to exactly one LineItem, preventing the same product from appearing in multiple orders.
findings.fix: Change the example to `LineItem "0..*" --> "1" Product : references`, unless an explicitly documented business constraint requires one-to-one product usage.
